ai.description: *Gekko nicobarensis* reaches 8 cm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal blotches and possesses distinct lateral skin folds for gliding. This endangered species is endemic to the Nicobar Islands.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gekko nicobarensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous lateral skin fold (patagium) along its flanks, which is absent in other Indian *Gekko* species.
ai.habitat: The Nicobar Gliding Gecko inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests within the Nicobar Islands, typically found on large trees at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar gliding gecko is primarily nocturnal and utilizes specialized skin flaps along its body to glide between trees, effectively escaping predators and foraging.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gekko nicobarensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, adhesive eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nicobar gliding gecko is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring primarily in lowland tropical forests from sea level to 200 meters.
